newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Skandia's shares rise on AFS unit sales. [CORRECTED 14:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Skandia's shares rise on AFS unit sales. [CORRECTED 14:40 GMT]

text.p: Shares in Swedish insurer Skandia rose on Thursday after its international life insurance unit Assurance and Financial Services (AFS) posted an 87 percent jump in 1996 sales in the U.S. to almost $2.8 billion, U.S. data showed.
(Corrects to add dropped words "in the U.S." to clarify that the figures refer to U.S. sales only and corrects currency from Swedish crowns).
"I cannot comment on single figures, but I know that there has been a very strong development in the U.S.," said Skandia spokesman Anders Lundblad.

In 1995, AFS's sales via its U.S. unit, American Skandia Life Assurance Co, amounted to $1.5 billion. (Corrects currency from Swedish crowns and adds dropped phrase "via its U.S. unit, American Skandia Life Assurance Co".)
The end of 1996 was a very strong period for AFS. AFS sales passed $2 billion at the start of October.
"The market has been very strong in 1996 and Skandia has continued to increase its market share," said one analyst.
Skandia shares rose on Thursday, partly on the back of the U.S. statistics that were published at the start of the week. At 1350 GMT its shares were 8.5 crowns higher at 229.5 crowns.
Analysts said there had been considerable interest from overseas investors in Skandia shares.
